description.narrative: Since January 2025, over 714,572 undocumented Afghans forcibly returned from Iran, 70% deported following Iran’s 20 March 2025 deadline for undocumented migrants to leave the country (UNHCR, June 2025). The majority enters Afghanistan at Islam Qala, Herat with a dramatic spike between 25–29 June with over 256,000 crossing, early July daily arrivals reached 43,000 ( IOM DTM 25) While previous returnees were mostly single men, current influx are entire families incl. unaccompanied minors, elderly, PWD, with increased protection risks like extortion and GBV (UN Women July 2025) Many arrive in extremely vulnerable conditions, having endured heat (40°C) and dust storms often with nothing but the clothes they are wearing. The IPC analysis (March–April 25) categorize returnees at Islam Qala in IPC Phase 4 or higher. Assessment by Cordaid and partner OHW at Islam Qala (10–15 June, 1-3 July 2025, verification 15 July 2025) with 30 community leaders (40% women), FGD with 120 returnees (50% female and unaccompanied minors), and observational data from reception points, shows over 80% of surveyed households lack access to food, clean water, shelter and health services. 90% of returnees has no access to hygiene products , 80% of surveyed households lack access to food, shelter, or means to pay transport to travel to area of origin which most plan. Humanitarian actors are responding but massive daily returns overwhelm available services with urgent need for scaled-up, multi-sectoral humanitarian support. Considering multiple urgent needs at Islam Qala and rapid market assessment (July 2025, OHW) confirming markets are functional , Cordaid& OHW will provide MPCA combined with WASH (Hygiene Awareness and Kit distribution) to address health risks for vulnerable groups in overcrowded unhygienic places in Islam Qala. The intervention will actively include protection mainstreaming by establishing help desks that can inform, advise and refer returnees to mitigate protection risks

The project targets undocumented returnees (100%) and specifically aims to include female-headed households (20% of HH), unaccompanied minors (over 5,000), pregnant and lactating women (50% malnourished, OHW, July 2025), elderly individuals (10%), and persons with disabilities (10%), who encounter increased risks of gender-based violence, exploitation, and health issues. Selection criteria include vulnerability assessments using Kobo Toolkit at reception points, focusing on risk like lack of income, dependency ratios, disability status, protection incidents, ensuring 50% of MPCA beneficiaries (1,628 HH) are from these groups. These groups will be actively supported and engaged by the help desks with male and female staff that provide information and referral to protection services of their need. Protection risk for these groups will be mitigated in delivery of MPC and Kits by consulting these groups on safe delivery measures.
